s1.syndrome_frame: Vasculitic syndrome with cutaneous and systemic involvement
salient_findings: Purpuric lesions on face, elbows, knees, and feet
Reticulated purpuric macules and patches on extensor surfaces
Skin sloughing off lesions on elbows and knees
key_facts: Patient is a woman in her 80s
History of nonischemic cardiomyopathy and chronic kidney disease
Presented with altered mental status after an unwitnessed fall
Purpuric lesions developed on nose, ear, and extensor surfaces of arms
Laboratory tests showed hypercalcemia and acute kidney injury
Rouleaux and cryoprotein precipitate on peripheral blood smear
Abnormal paraprotein band on serum and urine protein electrophoreses
Monoclonal IgG-κ protein on immunofixation electrophoresis
Elevated serum cryoglobulin levels
Biopsy showed intravascular fibrinoid material with cryoglobulins and fibrin thrombi
CT scan revealed lytic bony lesions
Bone marrow biopsy showed hypercellular marrow with 80% plasma cells and κ-light-chain restriction

shortlist.label: Multiple myeloma
shortlist.why_kept: Hypercalcemia, acute kidney injury, abnormal paraprotein band, monoclonal IgG-κ protein, and bone marrow biopsy showing hypercellular marrow with 80% plasma cells

shortlist.label: Type I cryoglobulinemic vasculitis
shortlist.why_kept: Purpuric lesions, elevated serum cryoglobulin levels, and biopsy showing intravascular fibrinoid material with cryoglobulins and fibrin thrombi

shortlist.label: Essential mixed cryoglobulinemia
shortlist.why_kept: Purpuric lesions, elevated serum cryoglobulin levels, and presence of cryoprotein precipitate on peripheral blood smear

shortlist.label: Waldenstrom macroglobulinemia
shortlist.why_kept: Abnormal paraprotein band, monoclonal IgG-κ protein, and presence of cryoprotein precipitate on peripheral blood smear

shortlist.label: Monoclonal gammopathy of undetermined significance
shortlist.why_kept: Abnormal paraprotein band, monoclonal IgG-κ protein, and presence of cryoprotein precipitate on peripheral blood smear

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation with purpuric lesions, elevated serum cryoglobulin levels, and biopsy findings of intravascular fibrinoid material with cryoglobulins and fibrin thrombi are consistent with Type I cryoglobulinemic vasculitis. Additionally, the presence of monoclonal IgG-κ protein and hypercellular marrow with 80% plasma cells on bone marrow biopsy suggests an underlying plasma cell dyscrasia, which is often associated with Type I cryoglobulinemia.

rejected.label: Multiple myeloma
rejected.why: While the patient has features of multiple myeloma, such as hypercalcemia, lytic bony lesions, and hypercellular marrow with plasma cell dyscrasia, the primary presentation of purpuric lesions and elevated cryoglobulin levels points more directly to a cryoglobulinemic vasculitis.

rejected.label: Essential mixed cryoglobulinemia
rejected.why: This condition typically involves a mix of monoclonal and polyclonal immunoglobulins, whereas the patient's immunofixation electrophoresis showed a monoclonal IgG-κ protein, suggesting Type I cryoglobulinemia.

rejected.label: Waldenstrom macroglobulinemia
rejected.why: This condition is characterized by the production of IgM monoclonal protein, which is not consistent with the patient's IgG-κ monoclonal protein.

rejected.label: Monoclonal gammopathy of undetermined significance
rejected.why: This condition is characterized by the presence of a monoclonal protein in the absence of end-organ damage, which is not the case in this patient with purpuric lesions, hypercalcemia, and acute kidney injury.
